\begin{theorem}[Logarithm of the reciprocal Gaussian density ratio]
\lean{FABL.log_inv_standardGaussianDensity_div}
\label{FABL.log_inv_standardGaussianDensity_div}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every real number $t>0$, the logarithm of the reciprocal of the standard Gaussian
density at $t$, divided by $t$, is $t^2/2 + \log t + \log\sqrt{2\pi}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Logarithmic growth of the reciprocal Gaussian density ratio]
\lean{FABL.log_inv_standardGaussianDensity_div_isEquivalent_sq}
\label{FABL.log_inv_standardGaussianDensity_div_isEquivalent_sq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.log_inv_standardGaussianDensity_div}
\difficulty{5}
As $t\to+\infty$, the logarithm of the reciprocal of the standard Gaussian density at
$t$, divided by $t$, is asymptotic to $t^2/2$.
\end{theorem}

Let $Z$ be a standard Gaussian random variable, and write $Q(t)=\mathbb{P}(Z>t)$ for its
upper-tail probability. As $t\to+\infty$, $\log(1/Q(t))$ is asymptotic to $t^2/2$,
meaning their ratio tends to $1$.
\end{theorem}
